sources.entry: Testing is not for beginners: why learning to test is hard. This shouldn't demotivate you though!

summary.title: Testing is Not for Beginners
summary.one_liner: Learning to write realistic tests while also learning to program is overwhelming for beginners, so the author argues it is better to learn testing after the basics of building things.
keywords: learn one thing at a time
takeaways: Beginners mostly write code that just works, so they usually cannot write realistic tests yet.
Simple tests like Add(2, 4) are useful for introducing testing but are not representative of real tests.
Learning programming, web development, and testing at the same time is a common cause of overwhelm and quitting.
The author recommends learning other skills first and returning to testing later, with a mentor helping if testing is learned early.
Revisiting old projects to redesign them with testing in mind is a way to learn testing later.
summary.summary: This opinion article by Jon Calhoun argues that testing is not a good first topic for beginner programmers. He explains that beginners focus on getting code to work, often write tangled code with global state and logic in views or controllers, and lack concepts like dependency injection and mocking needed for realistic tests. He compares learning testing alongside web development, HTTP, and other tools to being overwhelmed, and suggests learning other skills first and returning to testing later, with a soccer analogy used to make the point. The article is opinion-based and includes a small Go Add example and a PHP snippet as illustrations.
